about: The tracking plan (ADR 0036). Every feature asks which signal proves it is used and that it is worth it; every signal is here with the attributes it carries. Edit this file, then run `node tools/tracking-plan.mjs`: it writes docs/telemetry/tracking-plan.md and the frontend's event types. TrackingPlanTests holds the code to it at both ends.

features.name: Search
features.question: What share of typed searches finds nothing, and is it worse for agents than for people?
features.decision: Where the next relevance work goes: synonyms and golden-set queries for the empty ones, or the MCP tool's description if agents come back empty more often than people.

features.name: Browsing by category
features.question: Do people browse the taxonomy, or go straight to search?
features.decision: Whether the category pages earn their place in the navigation.

features.name: Product page
features.question: How do shoppers reach a product — a search, a category, the home page — and how many product views does a cart follow?
features.decision: Where discovery work goes: the search box, the taxonomy or the home page's rows.

features.name: Specs with their source
features.question: Do shoppers open the sentence behind a spec, and do they compare products side by side once they can?
features.decision: If nobody opens a source, the chip is decoration: keep the table, drop the chip's weight and spend review effort elsewhere. If comparisons are made and followed by a cart, the typed half of claims is worth its model and the next source (manuals, datasheets) is worth adding; if they are not, the comparison goes back to being a nice-to-have.

features.name: Cart
features.question: How many carts never become an order, and whose?
features.decision: Whether abandonment work (a saved cart, a reminder) comes before checkout friction.

features.name: Promotions
features.question: What share of orders carries a discount?
features.decision: Whether the promotion engine's combination rules are worth extending, or promotions stay a handful of codes.

features.name: Checkout and payment
features.question: Why does a checkout fail to become an order: a stale screen, a changed price, a declined card, or a provider that did not answer?
features.decision: A stale screen or a price change is our copy and our cache; a decline is the shopper's; an unavailable provider is ours to retry. Each points at a different fix.

features.name: Order page
features.question: Do shoppers come back to follow an order?
features.decision: None today.
features.gap: No decision depends on the answer: the page is the receipt, and it stays whatever the count is. A signal with no decision does not enter the plan.

features.name: Returns
features.question: Why do things come back?
features.decision: Wrong size and not-as-described are the product reasoning layer's case (phase 10); damaged and wrong item are the warehouse's.

features.name: Account and guest cart claim
features.question: Do guests sign in, and does their cart survive it?
features.decision: Whether guest checkout stays the default path.
features.gap: Not measured yet, and not planned: sign-in is the identity provider's, and the claim is one call with no screen of its own. Revisit when accounts do more than hold orders.

features.name: Review queue and publishing
features.question: Does the review queue move: how many drafts become products, and who approves them?
features.decision: Whether publishing needs bulk approval, and later whether the AI proposals of phase 10 are being approved or ignored.

features.name: Withdrawing a product
features.question: How often does a live product have to come back to review, and who pulls it?
features.decision: Whether withdrawing needs a recorded reason, as suspending an agent does, and whether imports should flag the changes that cause it.

features.name: Stock and reservations
features.question: How much held stock never becomes a sale?
features.decision: The hold's lifetime, and whether the expiry sweep the domain has a state for is worth building.

features.name: Catalogue import
features.question: Does an import bring products in?
features.decision: None beyond the run itself.
features.gap: An import is an operator's batch, answered by its own result and its span; a counter would say what the result already says.

features.name: Back-office administration
features.question: Are the orders, returns, promotions, attributes, variants, stock and audit screens used?
features.decision: None at three roles and a handful of users.
features.gap: Every write they make is already an audit row with its actor (ListAuditEntries): that is their evidence, and a metric would count the same thing twice.

features.name: WebMCP
features.question: Do browser agents use the shop's WebMCP tools, which ones, and do they succeed?
features.decision: Which tools to keep, extend or drop; a high share of refusals means a tool's contract is wrong for an agent.

features.name: MCP server and UCP catalogue
features.question: Do external agents call the catalogue over MCP and UCP, which tools, and how often are they refused?
features.decision: Whether the agent checkout of phase 11 has agents waiting for it, and which binding to build it on first.

features.name: AI search layer
features.question: How often is a search answered without one of its AI stages, and how many product changes did the vector layer miss?
features.decision: Whether the AI stages can be on by default, which service to fix first, and when a reindex is due.

features.name: Outbox
features.question: Is eventual consistency still eventual?
features.decision: When a second worker replica, and the row locking it needs, is worth building.

features.name: Claims from descriptions
features.question: How much of what a product's description states reaches the shopkeeper as a claim worth reviewing — and what is refused before they see it?
features.decision: A rising refusal rate for one reason points at one fix: not in the text is the prompt or the model, wrong language is the quantization (P10-0), a failed run is the model server. A queue that keeps failing on a product stops spending the model on it.

features.name: Claim review
features.question: Does the shopkeeper accept what the extractor proposes — and does reviewing the weakest first find the wrong ones?
features.decision: A falling approval rate means the extractor proposes what the shop would not say: revisit the prompt, the model or its settings before the queue stops being read.

features.name: Approved claims reach the catalogue
features.question: Does an approved typed claim become a catalogue attribute, or does Catalog refuse what Knowledge's vetting let through?
features.decision: Any refusal means the vetting and Catalog disagree on the vocabulary — a value vetting accepted that the definition does not: fix the vetting, never loosen the definition. Unchanged at a high rate means the extractor mostly restates attributes the import already set, and the typed half of the prompt is worth less than it costs.

features.name: Test orders
features.question: Do agents rehearse checkouts before they buy for real, and does every rehearsal end — none left holding stock?
features.decision: Rehearsals that are placed but never ended mean the saga stopped short and stock is held for nobody: fix the drain before anything else. Agents that go live without ever rehearsing are the ones whose first failures a customer pays for: make the test credential part of onboarding an agent (P11-3).

features.name: Agent registry
features.question: Do the agents that buy here come from operators the shop knows, or does money arrive through agents nobody registered?
features.decision: A growing share of placed orders from untrusted agents means the registry is not keeping up with who shops here: register the regular ones, and let the agent policy (P11-6) limit what an unknown agent may spend. Nothing from known agents means the registry is not worth its screen yet.

features.name: Shopkeeper dashboard
features.question: Does the shopkeeper start the day on the dashboard, and over which period do they read it?
features.decision: If the dashboard is opened less than the review queue it replaced as the home, the home goes back to the queue. A period nobody chooses is removed; widgets are reordered by what gets read, which is the v2 the task records.
features.gap: Reading is not a write, so there is no audit row, and the question is answered by what is already measured: every widget asks its own endpoint, so http.server.request.duration by route (/api/dashboard/*) and its period query parameter in the span count the openings per figure. A business counter would count the same requests a second time.

features.name: Backoffice jobs
features.question: Does the shopkeeper finish their jobs — publish, review a claim, ship, decide a return, suspend an agent — and how long does each take from opening its screen?
features.decision: A job whose time does not fall after the redesign goes back to R-3; a job that is refused more than it is done points at a screen that invites the wrong action. The before and after are the redesign article's evidence.

features.name: Agent rules
features.question: How often do the shop's own rules for agents refuse an order, which rule, and against agents of what trust?
features.decision: Refusals of known or verified agents by the cap mean the caps are too tight for the agents the shop wants: raise them. Refusals of untrusted agents are the rules working — and a rise in orders_per_hour from one trust level is the signal to look at who is looping. No refusals at all for a month means the rules are not earning their place in checkout's path.

events.name: webmcp_tool_invoked
events.description: A browser agent called one of the shop's WebMCP tools. Emitted with actor `webmcp`.

tool.description: The tool's registered name; never its arguments.

outcome.description: Refused is the shop saying no; failed is the tool breaking.

events.name: product_viewed
events.description: A shopper opened a product page. Only with analytics consent.

arrived_from.description: The page before this one, by kind; direct when there was none in this tab.

events.name: category_opened
events.description: A shopper opened a category listing (R-0 of the redesign). Only with analytics consent.

arrived_from.description: How the shopper got there: menu once the storefront has one (R-5), otherwise the kind of page before this one; direct when there was none in this tab. The kind and never the URL.

events.name: spec_source_opened
events.description: A shopper opened the words behind a spec — the quote and its support. Only with analytics consent.

source.description: Where the value came from; only a value an approved claim put there has words to open.

events.name: products_compared
events.description: A shopper opened a side-by-side comparison. Only with analytics consent.

products.description: How many products were compared, two to four.

events.name: backoffice_view_opened
events.description: The shopkeeper opened a backoffice screen (R-0 of the redesign). A staff event: sent by default under the shop's notice to staff, and never with who they are.

view.description: The screen, by its route; never an id in it.

events.name: backoffice_action_taken
events.description: The shopkeeper did what a screen is for — published, approved, shipped, decided, suspended — and how the server answered (R-0). A staff event.

view.description: The screen it was done on.

action.description: What was done, from a closed list.

outcome.description: done; refused when the server said no (a 4xx, a rule); failed when it could not answer.

metrics.name: tendero.search.degraded
metrics.description: Searches answered without one of their AI stages, by stage.

stage.description: The stage that did not answer.

metrics.name: tendero.search.vector_projection.failed
metrics.description: Product changes the vector layer could not take; the lexical index took them.

metrics.name: tendero.outbox.lag
metrics.description: Seconds between an event being raised and processed.

metrics.name: tendero.search.requests
metrics.description: Searches answered, by who asked, through what, typed or browsed, and whether anything came back.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

surface.description: The route the request came through. WebMCP inherits the shopper's session, so to the server it is the web; its evidence is `webmcp_tool_invoked`.

mode.description: Query when text was typed; browse when it was not — a category page, a home-page row.

category.description: Whether the search was narrowed to a category.

result.description: Whether the first page had any product.

metrics.name: tendero.carts.created
metrics.description: Carts opened. Against placed orders, it is abandonment: nothing sets a cart to Abandoned yet, so the difference is the measure.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

surface.description: The route the request came through. WebMCP inherits the shopper's session, so to the server it is the web; its evidence is `webmcp_tool_invoked`.

metrics.name: tendero.checkout.attempts
metrics.description: Every place-order attempt by its outcome; orders placed are the ones whose outcome is placed.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

surface.description: The route the request came through. WebMCP inherits the shopper's session, so to the server it is the web; its evidence is `webmcp_tool_invoked`.

order.mode.description: Test when the credential that placed it is a test one (ADR 0038): the Shop pulse leaves it out, and a rehearsal is read on its own.

agent.trust.description: How far the shop trusts the agent behind the attempt (P11-2): none for a person, untrusted for an agent nobody registered.

outcome.description: PlaceOrderOutcome, labelled by MetricLabels. not_mandated (P11-5): an agent's total outside what its verified mandate approved — how often agents try to spend what the person did not approve.

discounted.description: Whether any promotion applied to the order.

metrics.name: tendero.agents.denials
metrics.description: Agent orders the shop's own rules refused (P11-6), by rule and by how far the shop trusts the agent.

rule.description: The first rule in the table that denied.

agent.trust.description: The agent's standing in the registry; untrusted for one nobody registered.

metrics.name: tendero.orders.test_ended
metrics.description: Test orders that went all the way to confirmed and ended there, their stock given back.

metrics.name: tendero.returns.requested
metrics.description: Lines of the returns opened, by their reason: the closed set of five the domain keeps for exactly this analysis.

metrics.name: tendero.catalog.products.published
metrics.description: Products moved from Draft to Active.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

metrics.name: tendero.catalog.products.withdrawn
metrics.description: Products moved from Active back to Draft.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

metrics.name: tendero.inventory.reservations
metrics.description: Reservation transitions, by the state they reach.

status.description: ReservationStatus, labelled by MetricLabels. Expired is never recorded yet: nothing expires a hold.

metrics.name: tendero.agent.tool_calls
metrics.description: Calls from external agents to the MCP tools and the UCP catalogue operations.

surface.description: The binding the call came through.

tool.description: The tool or operation name; a closed set of the ones served.

outcome.description: Refused is the shop saying no; failed is the tool breaking.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.claims.proposed
metrics.description: Claims proposed for review, by the extractor that read the text.

extractor.description: Which extractor read the description: the rules, or the model.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.claims.dropped
metrics.description: Claims an extractor proposed that code refused before any person saw them, by reason.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.proposals.failed
metrics.description: Proposal runs that failed on a product; retried until its limit.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.descriptions.failed
metrics.description: Product changes whose description Knowledge could not record; the next save records it.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.claims.reviewed
metrics.description: Claims a person approved or rejected, by decision.

metrics.name: tendero.knowledge.claims.applied
metrics.description: Approved typed claims Catalog was asked to hold, by what it answered.
